mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or official corporate registrar in the foreign jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Luxembourg domestic sanctions lists, European Union restrictive measures, United Nations Security Council sanctions, US OFAC SDN list, FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists, Interpol notices, and World Bank debarment lists. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any politically exposed person (PEP), family member, or close associate, as well as any UBO or contributor resident in or conducting transactions from FATF-listed high-risk jurisdictions. Screening must be completed before name clearance and repeated within 15 days of incorporation.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_and_aml_profiling_note: For an SCSp, the beneficial owner is every individual who ultimately owns or controls more than 25% of the partnership, including through general or special partner interests, commission, or control rights. The RBE filing is made through the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) administered by the Luxembourg Business Registers. Access to the non-public section of the RBE is limited to competent authorities, certain obliged entities, and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) electronic filing portal: www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in one or more of the Luxembourg administrative languages (French, German, Luxembourgish) or, for international undertakings, may be submitted in a language using Latin script with a certified Latin-script transliteration. Names must not be misleading, must respect public order, and must not conflict with trademarks or existing rights. Use of a name containing non-Latin characters must be transliterated in the statutory filing and in all public extracts.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant must first request a written statement of reasons from the Luxembourg Business Registers. If the applicant disagrees, a formal application for review must be lodged with the RCS registration officer within 15 days of the refusal, annexing all supporting token-consent letters from ministries, regulatory bodies, trademark owners, or professional associations. If the review fails, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Luxembourg administrative tribunal within 40 days under the general rules of administrative procedure. A final judicial recourse lies before the Luxembourg Court of Appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual office without a physical presence is not permissible as a registered office for an SCSp in Luxembourg. Professional domiciliation agencies providing a physical Luxembourg address, physical mail handling, and access to office facilities are accepted. For the intended Government Affairs and Lobbying scope, the domiciliation must include administrative substance, a Luxembourg address at which official notices can be served, and a named person authorized to accept service. The RCS will reject any address that is merely a virtual mailbox or a non-existent location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of 12% to 18% in the first 12 months after incorporation. Unannounced on-site checks may be conducted by the Luxembourg Business Registers, the Public Prosecutor's Office, or tax/AML inspectors where there is any operational anomaly, negative PEP screening alert, or use of high-risk counterparties. The risk increases to approximately 35% if the SCSp is used for multi-jurisdictional lobbying payments.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 318-1 to 318-22 (special limited partnership); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2003 and Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the authority of the Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: SCSp constitution deed (acte de constitution) executed by private writing or notarial deed, submitted through the RCS e-Registration portal; the RCS registration extract constitutes the operative statutory filing instrument.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required for a Société en Commandite Spéciale; partner contributions are freely fixed in the partnership agreement and no escrow or blocked-account certificate is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the general partner has reviewed and by execution adopts the partnership agreement of Société en Commandite Spéciale, subscribing the initial partnership contribution and each partner's participation interest as set forth therein. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the SCSp be established at [address] in Luxembourg, and that any lease, servicing, or registered-agent letters be executed. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be appointed as general partner, manager and compliance officer, with sole authority to open bank accounts, make tax registrations, sign client engagement letters, and represent the SCSp before Luxembourg administrative authorities. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all formation filings be delegated to the appointed legal counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and pre-filing due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS name search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an availability search against RCS reserved and registered names. Ensure the name is not misleading and includes 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'. Prepare the draft SCSp partnership agreement (pacte social), including the general partner's unlimited liability, limited partner contribution provisions, profit-sharing waterfall, and Luxembourg registered office address.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name
Draft SCSp partnership agreement
Identity/passport copies of all general and limited partners
Proof of intended registered office address (lease or accommodation letter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, submit an alternative name application or file a written objection with the RCS registrar within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp constitution deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) or parties' private signature (sous seing privé) where notarial form is not mandatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the SCSp holds Luxembourg real property or the partnership agreement requires notarial form, execute before a Luxembourg notary. Otherwise execute the private written deed with qualified electronic signatures. All partners must sign, and the general partner must expressly accept its management mandate and unlimited liability.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement/constitution deed
Statement of acceptance by general partner
Proof of identity and capacity of each partner
Legalised/translated corporate authorisations for corporate partners, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If signature or capacity defects are discovered, execute a rectifying side deed or a new deed before RCS filing; notarial correction procedure applies where a notarial deed was used.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) e-Registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the signed deed, the general partner's acceptance, the registered office documentation, identity documents and any appointable natural person's declaration of non-conviction. Pay the RCS filing fee. The RCS verifies legal form, name, registered office, managers and statutory publication conditions and issues the registration extract.
required_dossiers: Signed SCSp deed or notarial certified copy
Declaration of non-conviction (déclaration sur l'honneur) of managers
Passport or national identity card of managers and partners
Registered office agreement signed by lessor or domiciliation agent
RCS e-registration application form
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a formal query, submit corrected instruments within 15 days. If registration is refused, appeal to the President of the Luxembourg District Court within one month from notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the electronic legal bulletin (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / Luxembourg Business Registers – Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the RCS automatically communicates the principal legal particulars for publication in RESA. Verify the published entry as to corporate name, date of deed, registered office, partners, general partner and managers. No separate submission is required, but the publication record should be retained as evidence against third parties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Confirmed publication order generated by LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication contains errors or omissions, file a written rectification request with RCS/LBR; in urgent cases obtain an interim order from the Luxembourg District Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Administration des Contributions Directes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a VAT registration application because cross-border consultancy and government-relations services may be subject to Luxembourg reverse-charge or local VAT rules. Request the Luxembourg national tax number, VAT number, and an EORI number if intra-Community transactions are anticipated. Disclose the SCSp's pass-through tax classification and the taxable position of the general partner.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
SCSp constitution deed
Identification and tax residence proof of the general partner
Declaration of forecast turnover and commencement date
Documentation of the Luxembourg office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT or tax number issuance is delayed beyond the statutory silence period, lodge a reminder with AEDT; if rejected, appeal to the tax administration's director within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operational establishment and occupation compliance filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy / Commission des Autorisations d'Établissement; Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); Administration de la Sécurité Civile
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the lobbying and government-relations consultancy requires a business establishment permit under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the freedom of establishment. If not exempt, file the autorisation d'établissement application. Submit the office occupancy title, floor plan showing emergency exits and sanitary facilities, professional liability insurance, and workplace risk assessment. Register the workplace with ITM if employees will be engaged.
required_dossiers: Establishment permit application form (Formulaire autorisation d'établissement)
Lease agreement or title to commercial office premises
Floor plan with fire-safety and evacuation features
Professional indemnity and public liability insurance certificates
Workplace risk assessment and emergency plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment permit application is queried, provide additional documents within 15 days. If refused, lodge an administrative appeal with the Ministry of the Economy or the Administrative Tribunal within one month.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des PME et de l'Entrepreneuriat, Commission des Autorisations d'Établissement
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement pour l'activité de conseil en affaires et relations gouvernementales (Commercial Establishment Permit for Government Relations Advisory)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (AEV) – Luxembourg Environment Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Exempt – no mandatory full EIA is required for an office-based lobbying and policy advisory operation, provided the municipality confirms the premises may be used for administrative/consulting activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater or process VOC emissions are generated. Office wastewater must comply with the Luxembourg Grand-Ducal Waste Water Regulation, including municipal sewer discharge limits. Any solvent-containing products must respect EU VOC Directive 2004/42/EC limits. Office waste, including paper, electronics, and non-hazardous waste, must be segregated and collected by approved waste operators in accordance with the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate obtained from the Administration de la Sécurité Civile / Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours; office lease occupancy certification confirming permitted administrative use; structural load assessment not separately required for a standard office lease; occupational clearance through Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering workplace safety, first-aid equipment, emergency lighting, ventilation, and occupational risk assessment for staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; official portals: myguichet.lu, impotsdirects.public.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign investors forming a Luxembourg SCSp must first register constitutional documents with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through a local notary or legal agent, obtain the national identification number (matricule), then apply for the NIF and VAT number via MyGuichet.lu using Forms 102/845; a non-resident SCSp is also required to register for VAT without delay once it makes taxable supplies in Luxembourg or acquires a taxable nexus. Registration is completed when economic activity commences or when a Luxembourg VAT-obligated transaction is first carried out.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election is available; Luxembourg SCSp is fiscally transparent by statute for corporate income tax and net wealth tax. Available elections include: (i) application to form or join a VAT group (assujetti unique) with other Luxembourg taxable persons; (ii) waiver of the small-enterprise VAT exemption; and (iii) election to apply the Ordinary VAT regime for rental/receivables activities. There is no hybrid mismatch election for this partnership unless ATAD/CFC rules are separately implemented at partner level.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Luxembourg-resident small undertakings: €35,000 annual taxable turnover (excl. VAT) is the exemption/registration threshold under the small business scheme; non-resident SCSp has no turnover threshold and must register for VAT as soon as it supplies taxable goods or services in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory API extraction, or digital stamping applies to B2B VAT invoices. Electronic invoicing to Luxembourg public contracting bodies is mandatory via Peppol BIS 3.0/EN16931. B2B electronic invoicing is permitted but optional, and VAT returns are filed separately through the normal AEDT electronic portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations qualify for 0% VAT if goods are physically transported outside the EU and proved by a customs export declaration; intra-EU supplies can be zero-rated when the customer supplies a valid EU VAT identification number and the EC Sales List is filed; certain lobbying and policy advisory services performed for non-EU or foreign business clients fall outside Luxembourg VAT under B2B place-of-supply rules, making Luxembourg VAT inapplicable and any input VAT recoverable under the supplier's normal business activity.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg VAT administration may require complete export evidence (customs declarations, transport contracts, B/L/AWB, bank transfer and payment advisory) before sustaining a 0% rate; failure to substantiate leads to retrospective VAT clawback at 17%, monthly default interest up to 0.8%, administrative fines for incomplete or inaccurate records, and criminal penalties for falsification or VAT fraud of up to €250,000 and/or five years' imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), the Ministry of Finance, and the European System of Central Banks / ECB framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a eurozone Member State; the euro is fully convertible. Both current-account flows and, save for EU/EEA gold-plating measures, capital-account flows are liberalised for cross-border transactions arising from the freedom of movement of capital under EU primary law. Profit remittances from a transparent Luxembourg SCSp are not subject to withholding tax at the partnership level; distributions to non-resident partners are free from exchange-control restrictions and may be made in EUR or any freely convertible currency, subject only to standard bank AML/CTF verification and applicable tax declarations. No prior central-bank approval is required for capital subscriptions, retainer fee repatriation, or liquidation proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg law imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline for export receipts or service-policy advisory fees. Foreign-currency accounts may be maintained freely at CSSF-regulated credit institutions; BCL statistical balance-of-payments reporting is limited to national statistical posting and does not restrict the holding or disposition of foreign-exchange receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
Quintet Private Bank (formerly KBL European Private Bankers)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Luxembourg-regulated Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and EU/EEA passporting EMIs can support SEPA/euro settlement, multi-currency transaction accounts, and cross-border wire issuance, but they cannot lawfully provide full commercial credit, complex escrow, or investment-grade treasury instruments. For a Luxembourg SCSp engaged in cross-border trade-policy advisory and government-affairs lobbying, a foreign/EU EMI is suitable only for low-value operating disbursements and petty-cash management; it is not an adequate substitute for a Tier-1 Luxembourg credit institution with respect to capital escrow, large retainer collection, or FX hedging under bank confirmations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In almost all Tier-1 Luxembourg banks, a physical onboarding meeting with the general partner (or formally appointed authorised manager) is expected at the bank's Luxembourg offices. Remote opening may be permitted under CSSF video-KYC guidelines if the general partner holds a valid EU/EEA eIDAS-certified identity or the bank accepts a notarised power of attorney with a face-to-face interview of the local authorised signatory; nevertheless, because the business scope is government-affairs lobbying and the entity structure is a non-corporate special limited partnership with non-resident partners, the bank's compliance committee will normally require at least one physical interview with the natural-person general partner or the fiduciary manager before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial-ownership chain caused by the SCSp's contractual nature and the anonymity of limited partners (names not published in the Luxembourg RCS).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete beneficial-ownership matrix identifying every natural-person ultimate owner, each partner's economic interest and control rights; a certified copy of the partnership agreement (contrat de société), all side letters and deeds amending the agreement; a Luxembourg legal opinion confirming the SCSp's valid formation, capacity, and economic substance; and a signed AML/CTF declaration for the general partner and each direct limited partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated political-exposure risk inherent in the lobbying / government-affairs advisory sector, especially where foreign stakeholders or former public officials are involved.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full PEP and public-official declarations for all partners, senior managers, and key beneficiaries; comprehensive CVs and professional records demonstrating employment and background; a copy of the firm's registration on the Luxembourg and/or European Union transparency registers and any statutory lobbying licence; written confirmation from the commercial client explaining the retainer mandate; and two substantive professional references from a regulated bank or law firm certifying fourteen years of commercial record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound wire transfers from non-transparent or tax-preferred jurisdictions and inconsistent source-of-wealth documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six to twelve months of original international bank statements for each source account; audited or unaudited financial statements of material contributors; tax residence certificates of each source jurisdiction; legally documented commercial contracts, invoices, and engagement letters underlying each inbound retainer or capital contribution; and sworning affidavits by the ultimate economic owners describing the accumulated wealth and the exact financial path inbound to the SCSp.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perception of letterbox status or lack of real economic substance in Luxembourg in light of the transparency-pass-through classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed Luxembourg office lease and proof of physical occupation; payroll records and Luxembourg social-security filings for resident employees; board/management minutes showing real decision-making; the SCSp's Luxembourg VAT identification certificate if applicable; a realistic annual budget and business plan aligned with ISIC 7020 government-relations advisory; and tax accounting records evidencing the partner capital structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from non-Luxembourg partners must be routed through a CSSF-regulated credit institution via SWIFT MT103 (single investor) or MT202/MT202COV (treasury-concentrated settlement) with strict compliance preparation. The remitter must use the BCL statistical purpose code appropriate to a direct equity injection (typically D610 for direct investment capital or, for certain fund-architecture flows, D620) and must include in the narrative the SCSp's full legal name, the Luxembourg RCS registration number, and the phrase 'partnership capital contribution / no consideration invoiced'. Before the first wire, the account officer and compliance team require the final approved KYC file, an incoming-funds questionnaire, and a copy of the board/general-partner resolution approving the subscription. Payments from unregulated third-party payers or from jurisdictions on the FATF grey list are blocked unless a prior case-by-case protective review is completed and documented.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For recurring advisory-fee settlements to EU/EEA beneficiary bank accounts, the platform rail is SEPA Credit Transfer (X1/XML pain.001) using the beneficiary's IBAN and BIC, with the required purpose and reference text for VAT/accounting traceability. For non-EUR and rest-of-world payments, the applicable rail is SWIFT MT103 via a correspondent banking network; where the disbursement supports trade documents or subcontracting of foreign trade-policy services, a commercial irrevocable letter of credit may be issued under UCP600/ISBP745 to ensure documentary compliance. All outbound wires must be pre-screened by the bank's AML engine, and counterparty SSIs should be verified using a validated SWIFT/ISO 20022 standing-information source or an independent bank-to-bank confirmation to mitigate fraud and clearing error.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF deliverable FX forwards (FXA) with CSSF-authorised bank counterparties under a duly executed ISDA Master Agreement.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies only if the counterparty is a qualifying EEA credit institution or an equivalent third-country/OECD regulated entity and the NDF is booked with clear underlying exposure, trade reporting under EMIR, and no outsize leverage.
Currency options (European-style puts and calls) purchased as hedges for specific retainer or capital flows, with protocol-covered transaction confirmations.

Cross-currency swaps (CS) for matching dual-currency partnership subscriptions and periodic distribution liabilities, subject to EMIR clearing obligations, margin rules, and trade repository reporting to the Luxembourg competent authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual registration confirmation (confirmation annuelle) of RCS data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following the anniversary of RCS registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of EUR 250; repeated non-compliance may trigger administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of Beneficial Owner (RBE) register data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 January and 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 25,000; per-day penalty of EUR 125 for late confirmation under certain circumstances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing and publication of annual accounts (only if statutory thresholds met; otherwise prepared and kept internally)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS / Recueil électronique des sociétés (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the financial year, followed by RESA publication within one month of filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False declaration or late filing fines up to EUR 10,000; potential civil liability of general partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Business Tax (impôt commercial communal) annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May following the tax year (or within six months after taxpayer’s year-end if different)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge up to 10% of tax due; default interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual economic substance declaration (if activity is not deemed substantive)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg direct tax administration (ACD) via annual corporate income tax formalities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May following the fiscal year (with possible extension)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Rebuttable presumption of non-substance; penalties for insufficient substance combined with cross-border transactions may reach EUR 250,000.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: SCSp is exempt from statutory audit unless it meets two of three thresholds: balance sheet total > EUR 4.4M, net turnover > EUR 8.8M, average workforce > 50 employees; audit is also mandatory if all general partners are legal persons or if required by the partnership agreement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Chart of Accounts based on the Luxembourg Commercial Code) as transposed under the EU Accounting Directive; IFRS permitted for consolidated accounts and certain large entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Before March 31 each year, all SCSp general and limited partners must be reviewed as potential beneficial owners; any shareholding transfer or control change must be updated in the RBE register within 21 days of becoming known, and the annual confirmation attests the continued accuracy of this data.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and General Partners

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Ranges from USD 2,000 to USD 6,000 per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 to USD 20,000 (only if audit thresholds triggered)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined statutory rate (17% corporate income tax + 1.19% unemployment fund contribution calculated as 7% of the 17% IRC + 6.75% municipal business tax in Luxembourg City; municipal rate varies by commune from 6.75% to 11.9%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default (no legal personality): entity-level corporate income tax is nil where the vehicle is not a commercial opco, and each partner is taxed at their residence. Where Luxembourg CIT becomes applicable (recharacterization or commercial activity), the participation exemption (100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains), IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income, effective ~5.25%), commercial video game tax credit (up to 25% of eligible expenses), and digital R&D tax credit (up to 20%) reduce the effective burden. Note: Luxembourg statutory loss carryforward is indefinite under LIR Art. 110; the 5-year limit applied in this dossier is a conservative model benchmark.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Déclaration commune pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, l'impôt commercial communal et l'impôt sur la fortune) filed electronically via the eCDF module on MyGuichet.lu / RTS (Registre des Taxes) of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (financial year basis; calendar tax year unless a different accounting period of maximum 12 months has been approved by the ACD).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before 31 December of the calendar year following the relevant fiscal year (Art. 161 LIR), i.e., within 12 months after the fiscal year-end; the ACD commonly grants a two-to-three-month extension on written request. Quarterly prepayments are due on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RCS registration number, legal form (SCSp), registered office address, fiscal year-end date, and VAT identification number if separately registered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate name and tax identification number of the appointed Luxembourg tax representative; declare the transparent status so that no entity-level CIT is assessed on pass-through income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the tax year; maximum period of 12 months; state the calendar year unless a different accounting date has been approved in writing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the partner allocation schedule with each foreign partner's home fiscal year to avoid mismatched loss or income recognition in treaty relief claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net book profit or loss of the commercial activity per the statutory balance sheet before tax, inclusive of lobbying retainer income, advisory fees, and any foreign stakeholder engagement revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Luxembourg-situs business income with an attached functional analysis evidencing the SCSp's local decision-making, staff, and risk assumption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory add-backs: 50% of representation and restaurant costs, fines, corporate income tax payments, gifts exceeding EUR 100 per recipient, and interest on unpaid taxes (LIR Arts. 45 and 48).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should not duplicate these add-backs in the Luxembourg schedule where the same costs have already been disallowed in the home jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable income after participation exemption, IP box relief, investment reserve (Art. 110bis LIR), and loss carryforward set-off; this figure feeds the partner allocation schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a transparent SCSp, do not self-assess CIT at entity level in this line; the amount is informative for municipal business tax (IBT) exposure and withholding tax analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement on whether the SCSp exercises a commercial, industrial or craft activity within Luxembourg; used to determine municipal business tax and permanent establishment status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign general partner exercising management functions in Luxembourg may create a Luxembourg permanent establishment; file a protective IBT declaration to avoid dual assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file: administrative fine up to EUR 3,750 per return (Art. 224 LIR) and immediate official assessment (taxation d'office) with a 10% surcharge on the assessed tax where the return is omitted, incomplete, or imprecise. Late payment: statutory interest at 1.2% per quarter on arrears. Deliberate false returns escalate to tax fraud (Art. 226 LIR): fine up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; 0% applies under the participation exemption regime where a qualifying EU parent or a corporate partner holding at least 10% for 12 months receives the dividend; for a transparent SCSp, ordinary profit allocations to partners are partnership distributions, not dividends, and are generally outside the WHT net.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident partners claiming double-taxation agreement (DTA) relief must: (1) obtain an original residence certificate (TRC) for the relevant calendar year from the partner's tax administration; (2) submit Form 22 (Rückerstattungs-/Entlastungsantrag) to the ACD before or within one year of the distribution; (3) provide a beneficial-ownership declaration and a substance memorandum demonstrating that the SCSp is not an MLI conduit; (4) attach dividend vouchers and distribution statements. The ACD applies a strict principal-purpose test under the MLI and denies relief absent genuine economic activity, risk, and staff in Luxembourg.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rate is 0% on both royalty and interest payments made by a Luxembourg entity to non-residents; the domestic exemption eliminates source tax, so treaty rates (typically 0% for interest and 5-10% for royalties under many DTAs) are rarely invoked; no registration or ACD pre-clearance is required for such payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg Local File / Master File documentation is triggered when aggregate related-party transactions exceed EUR 10,000,000 for goods or EUR 1,000,000 for services, financial transactions, and management fee recharges; Country-by-Country reporting is mandatory for groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations code; substance is enforced through LIR Art. 168 anti-abuse provisions, the ATAD general anti-avoidance rule, administrative TP circulars requiring a functions-risks-assets analysis, and the MLI principal-purpose test. A bare SCSp without a Luxembourg-based general partner, local staff, or substantive board decision-making is recharacterized as a letterbox shell, with treaty benefits denied, the corporate veil pierced, and source taxation reimposed at the 15% dividend WHT rate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of partner profit shares, fabrication of deductible expenses in the lobbying retainer chain, use of undocumented cash wires, or sham back-to-back loan structures between the SCSp and foreign related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restitution of the entire evaded tax in cash; interest at 1.2% per quarter; criminal fine up to EUR 50,000; imprisonment up to 5 years (Art. 226 LIR); publication of the judgment and prohibition from holding public office in Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant or general partner may be declared joint debtor for the unpaid tax where fraud or gross negligence is proven (veil-piercing); travel bans, asset freezes, and preventive detention may be ordered pending criminal proceedings.
